detail.title: The Role of Technology in Improving Entrepreneurial Relationships with MSME Actors in the Ketapang Housing Complex, Gowa Regency
detail.abstract: Digital transformation has become a new pattern in entrepreneurship. This study aims to analyze the role of digital technology in strengthening entrepreneur relationships in the Ketapang residential area, Gowa Regency, and to identify factors that influence the effectiveness of its implementation. The research approach used is descriptive qualitative with in-depth interviews and focus group discussions (FGD) with MSME actors operating in the area. Data analysis was conducted thematically to explore the relationship between digitalization, digital literacy, social capital, and business performance. The results of the study show that the use of digital platforms such as WhatsApp Business, Facebook, Instagram, and e-commerce, as well as payment transaction tools such as Qris, Dana, Gopay, and Ovo, has strengthened business networks, expanded market access, and improved the effectiveness of communication between business actors. Digital literacy has been proven to play a mediating role in strengthening digitalization to improve MSME performance. Meanwhile, supporting factors such as internet infrastructure and community support are important elements that determine success. Research confirms that strengthening the environment plays an important role in maintaining entrepreneurial sustainability. A triple helix between local government, educational institutions, and local communities is needed to create a sustainable technology-based entrepreneurial ecosystem. By involving the entire community, digitization not only functions as an economic instrument but also as a means of social empowerment and strengthening local economic solidarity.

affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt - Department of Money and Macroeconomics and Deutsche Bundesbank

detail.title: Peering Beyond the Veil: A Dissection of Aggregate Bank Lending Rate Movements Into Pricing and Composition Effects Using Credit-level Data

publicationDetails.journalName: Deutsche Bundesbank Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Compared to 2021, the aggregate bank lending rate to firms in the euro area increased strongly during the monetary tightening and easing cycle of 2022-25. However, it rose up to 1.5 percentage points less than the rise in policy and money market rates. We approach this gap using granular credit registry data, revealing how changes in the composition and pricing of credit translate into developments of the aggregate rate. The tool we use is standard in labor economics, but scarcely used outside that context: the Oaxaca-Blinder decomposition. We are the first to apply it to analyze the development of an aggregate variable over time in the loan pricing literature. We find that changes in the pricing of credit compared to 2021 were the main reason why a gap opened up. Compositional shifts in firm and credit characteristics and changes in banks’ market shares had minor effects. Our microlevel insights have implications for policy makers, bankers and debtors, as they help understand what shapes aggregate pass-through patterns and the strength of monetary policy transmission. Moreover, our approach opens up promising new applications in the loan supply literature.

title: Operationalizing Trust: A Five-Step Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Governance Framework for Generative AI in Banking

detail.title: Operationalizing Trust: A Five-Step Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) Governance Framework for Generative AI in Banking
detail.abstract: As financial institutions strive to adopt Generative AI (GenAI) within highly regulated environments, they face a dual threat: the operational risk of "Shadow AI", unsanctioned tool usage by employees, and the compliance risk of non-deterministic model outputs. While the industry seeks to leverage Large Language Models (LLMs) for efficiency, strict regulatory frameworks (e.g., NYDFS Part 500, EU AI Act) demand a level of auditability and accuracy that "black box" models cannot inherently provide. This paper proposes a novel, operational governance framework: The TRUST Model (Triage, Review, Underwrite, Strengthen, Track). Designed specifically for regulated environments, this five-step cycle allows institutions to leverage the speed of AI while maintaining the judgment of human experts. We demonstrate how this approach enables institutions to deploy sanctioned, compliant AI alternatives that satisfy regulatory scrutiny, effectively displacing Shadow AI with a governed, self-improving system.

title: Rebuilding the Frontier: A Property Rights and Sustainable Materials Strategy for China's Next Development Cycle
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Rebuilding the Frontier: A Property Rights and Sustainable Materials Strategy for China's Next Development Cycle
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the intertwined challenges of regional disparity, demographic outflow, and unsustainable urban development in China by proposing a transformative national strategy centered on the development of sustainable singlefamily housing (SFH) in frontier regions. We identify the lack of secure, long-term property rights as a core impediment to reversing the decline of the Northeast, Northwest, and Southwestern frontiers, echoing Adam Smith's classical insight on the link between property rights and land improvement. Our model integrates two pillars: (1) the grant of perpetual, tradable land use rights within designated Frontier Revitalization Zones, creating a powerful incentive for household investment and population inflow; and (2) the mandatory use of modern engineered timber and sustainable building materials, serving as an environmental safeguard, a catalyst for a green industrial policy, and a means of cultural renewal. Through a multidimensional site selection matrix, we identify six pilot regions-Dalian, Ili Valley, Jinzhou, Jiuquan, Nyingchi (Linzhi), and the Urumqi Plains-representing a diverse portfolio for testing and implementation. We argue that this strategy is not a real estate stimulus, but a systemic intervention designed to trigger a virtuous cycle of capital flow, community formation, and fiscal sustainability, ultimately securing China's frontiers and establishing a new paradigm for high-quality, distributed development.

title: A Compliance-Aware Artificial Intelligence Framework for Autonomous Reliability Management in Financial Software-as-a-Service Cloud Environments

detail.title: A Compliance-Aware Artificial Intelligence Framework for Autonomous Reliability Management in Financial Software-as-a-Service Cloud Environments
detail.abstract: This study introduced an AI framework that automates Level-1 and Level-2 Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) operations in financial Software-as-a- Service (SaaS) clouds. The framework integrates Vertex AI and Kubernetes to automate anomaly detection, diagnosis, and correction with auditable governance logs. Using a mixed empirical design that combines production telemetry analysis with controlled simulations, the system reduced MTTR by 70% and SLA breaches by 25%. The results confirm that autonomy and compliance can coexist within regulated environments, advancing AI-driven reliability engineering. This research closes a persistent gap in unifying automation with verifiable compliance, offering a replicable foundation for improving reliability while maintaining governance.

detail.title: Forecasting Inflation: The Sum of the Cycles Outperforms the Whole

publicationDetails.detailsText: Bank of Finland Research Discussion Paper No. 1/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: Bank of Finland Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Inflation dynamics reflect forces operating at different cycles, from short-lived shocks to long-term structural trends. We introduce the sum-of-the-cycles (SOC) method, which exploits this multifrequency structure of inflation for forecasting. SOC decomposes inflation into cyclical components, applies forecasting models suited to their persistence, and recombines them into an aggregate forecast. Across U.S. inflation measures and horizons, SOC consistently outperforms leading time-series benchmarks, reducing forecast errors by about 25 percent at short horizons and nearly 50 percent at long horizons. During the 2020-21 inflation surge, when many models – including advanced machine-learning methods – struggled, SOC retained strong performance by incorporating shortage indicators. Beyond accuracy, SOC enhances interpretability: financial variables dominate high- and business-cycle frequencies, Phillips Curve models are most informative at medium frequencies, and factor-based methods, forecast combinations, and shortage indices prevail at low frequencies. This combination of accuracy and transparency makes SOC a practical complement to existing tools for inflation forecasting and policy analysis.

title: Blockchain Technology Applications in Environmental Science: A Comprehensive Literature Review
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Blockchain Technology Applications in Environmental Science: A Comprehensive Literature Review
detail.abstract: Environmental sustainability faces unprecedented challenges requiring transformative technological interventions. Blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for addressing transparency, traceability, and trust deficits across carbon markets, waste management, supply chains, renewable energy, and conservation finance. This systematic literature review synthesizes 380+ peerreviewed publications spanning 2015-2025, examining blockchain's theoretical foundations, practical implementations, and future trajectories across environmental domains. Key findings reveal that while blockchain demonstrates significant potential-reducing carbon credit verification times by 60% and enabling 99.95% energy consumption reductions through consensus mechanism transitions-substantial gaps remain in scalability, interoperability, and regulatory harmonization that must be addressed before widespread deployment.

title: Interest Rate Transmission in India (2005–2024): A Long-Term Analysis

detail.title: Interest Rate Transmission in India (2005–2024): A Long-Term Analysis
detail.abstract:
Interest rate transmission is central to modern monetary policy. This study evaluates how India’s policy rate changes influenced lending rates, deposit rates, credit conditions, and macroeconomic outcomes over a nineteen-year period. Using secondary data from the central bank and official financial publications, the paper analyzes transmission through the interest rate channel, credit channel, liquidity channel, and expectations channel.

The findings indicate that transmission was historically slow and incomplete due to structural rigidities in the banking system. However, transmission strengthened after the introduction of the Marginal Cost of Funds Based Lending Rate (MCLR) in 2016 and became significantly faster and more transparent after the shift to external benchmark lending rates (EBLR) in 2019. The study concludes by identifying the reforms that improved transmission efficiency and highlights remaining challenges in the Indian monetary system.

affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria

detail.title: Impact of inflation on financial inclusion: a global and regional analysis
detail.abstract: This study investigates the effect of inflation on the accessibility dimension of financial inclusion across 61 countries. The consumer price index and the GDP implicit price deflator are used as measures of inflation. Four accessibility indicators of financial inclusion are used which are the composite financial inclusion index, the number of bank depositors, ATM penetration and the number of bank branches. Using the median quantile regression and the two-stage least squares regression methods, the findings reveal that inflation has a positive effect on financial inclusion in European countriaes. A one percent increase in inflation leads to at least a 0.05 percent increase in financial inclusion in Europe. A negative but insignificant effect was found in African, Asian and the Americas countries. The moderation analysis shows that banking sector stability does not weaken the adverse effect of inflation on financial inclusion in African countries, but a high loan-to-deposit ratio in the banking sector weakens the adverse effect of inflation on financial inclusion and accelerates financial inclusion in a high inflation environment in African countries. In the individual mechanism analysis, we find that inflation decreases the number of bank depositors in the Americas and increases the number of bank depositors in European countries. High inflation decreases financial inclusion through a decrease in the number of bank branches in African and European countries. The implication of the findings is that inflation adversely affect financial inclusion, and the effect depend on the financial access indicator being examined. Policymakers need to identify the financial access indicators that are worst hit by rising inflation, and they should explore how monetary policy tools can reduce inflation persistence without decreasing the level of financial inclusion.

title: From Hardship to Hope: Post-Pandemic Realities and Resilient Journeys of Low-Income Migrant Women in India

detail.title: From Hardship to Hope: Post-Pandemic Realities and Resilient Journeys of Low-Income Migrant Women in India
detail.abstract: The study examines the impact of the pandemic on low-income migrant women workers in India, focusing on four main themes: "decent work," "decent living," "skill development," and "women’s empowerment." This study proposes a feasible longitudinal extension to track into work conditions, housing, education, and medical facilities for these workers. It highlights how increased social media usage during the pandemic facilitated skill development, empowering women to seek better jobs or start their own ventures. Additionally, it discusses the roles of social media, self-dependency, and decision-making among these women. The study evaluates the economic, social, and psychological impacts on 30 women aged 18 to 45, working in various sectors like domestic help, construction, housekeeping, and sales. It underscores the challenges faced by this vulnerable group and government interventions to address their needs, shedding light on their resilience amidst adversity.

As a result, MB became a second largest political force in Egypt, although it remained banned till January 25 Revolution. detail.abstract: This paper examines how the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) will affect the accuracy of corporate financial reporting through the investigation of trends and performance in the mandatory disclosures of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). To fill a research gap, it quantitatively analyzes three areas: the commonality and the increase in GenAI disclosure across industries, the relationship between disclosure intensity and financial reporting performance, and the most dominant thematic tendencies in risk fictions. Using a secondary data analysis format, the study systematically examines text information of thousands of SEC 10-K reports and compares it with financial performance data of Audit Analytics, including industry controls and an evidence synthesis of regulatory reports. The results indicate an evolutionary change: AI and GenAI references in corporate reports increased by more than 150% and 350%, respectively, between 2022 and 2024, and the discussion was extensively provided in the material risk context. Ostensibly, a statistically significant negative correlation was found between the frequency of GenAI keywords usage in disclosures and the incidence of financial restatements. Firms that framed AI in a strategic, benefit-oriented setting had the most moderate restatement. The research adds to the literature that presents the first extensive empirical data on the connection between certain characteristics of AI disclosure and objective financial reporting quality. It provides valuable lessons to regulators working on disclosure guidelines, to auditors trying to accommodate AI-driven processes, and to corporate managers who want to use AI to provide better reporting integrity and governance.

detail.title: Understanding Immigrant Self-Employment in Sweden: Insights from the Literature

declarations.funderStatement: The author is thankful for financial support from Jan Wallanders och Tom Hedelius Stiftelse, project P16-0192 and P23-0186.

publicationDetails.journalName: Research Institute of Industrial Economics (IFN) Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We present results from research on different dimensions of immigrant self-employment in Sweden. There are variations in self-employment rates between different groups of immigrants and the native population. Self-employment rates have increased markedly among certain groups of immigrants since the 1990s. Immigrants from certain countries in the Middle East are over-represented in self-employment, while self-employment rates among immigrants from countries in Africa are relatively low. Immigrants from countries outside Europe are often selfemployed in branches with low entry barriers. Exit rates from self-employment are generally higher and earnings are lower among self-employed non-European immigrants than among self-employed natives and European immigrants. Research regarding explanations for why immigrants opt for self-employment is presented. Results indicate that immigrants are pushed into self-employment due to low earnings in wage-employment. As regards the effects of ethnic enclaves, networks and traditions from their home countries, the results are inconclusive. Family traditions and parental role models increase self-employment propensities more for immigrants than for natives. Non-European immigrants report that they encounter other difficulties and obstacles in their business activities than natives and European immigrants. They consider lack of access to financial capital and discrimination from banks, customers, and suppliers as obstacles for successful self-employment. Finally, results show that immigrants who are successful in their business activities may play an important role for labor market integration since they create employment opportunities also for other immigrants.

detail.abstract: We study how students adjust their early career choices in response to economic crises and how these decisions affect their long-run labor market outcomes. Focusing on Sweden's deep recession in the early 1990s-which hit the manufacturing and construction sectors hardest-we first show that students whose fathers lost jobs in these sectors were more likely to choose career paths tied to less-affected industries. These students later experienced better labor market outcomes, including higher employment and earnings. Our findings suggest that informational frictions are a key obstacle to structural change and identify career choice as an important channel through which recessions reshape labor markets in the long run.

title: Density Forecast Transformations
affiliations: Banque de France and Banco de España

detail.title: Density Forecast Transformations
detail.abstract: The popular choice of using a direct forecasting scheme implies that the individual predictions ignore information on their cross-horizon dependence. However, this dependence is needed if the forecaster has to construct, based on direct density forecasts, predictive objects that are functions of several horizons (e.g. when constructing annual-average growth rates from quarter-on-quarter growth rates). To address this issue, we propose to use copulas to combine the individual h-step-ahead predictive distributions into a joint predictive distribution. Our method is particularly appealing to practitioners for whom changing the direct forecasting specification is too costly. In a Monte Carlo study, we demonstrate that our approach leads to a better approximation of the true density than an approach which ignores the potential dependence. We show the superior performance of our method in several empirical examples, where we construct (i) quarterly forecasts using month-on-month direct forecasts, (ii) annual-average forecasts using monthly year-on-year direct forecasts, and (iii) annual-average forecasts using quarter-on-quarter direct forecasts.

title: A Mindset-Based Paradigm for Brand Definition: Introducing the Bigi Model
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: A Mindset-Based Paradigm for Brand Definition: Introducing the Bigi Model

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest, financial or personal, related to this research.

declarations.funderStatement: No funding was received for this study.

detail.abstract: Over the past two decades, branding has evolved into a multidimensional discipline shaped by developments in consumer psychology, organizational behaviour, and experiential marketing. (Aaker, 1996; Keller, 1993; Schmitt, 1999) Yet, despite this evolution, a significant conceptual gap persists: many organizations still approach branding through external artefacts rather than internal foundations. (Kapferer, 2012; Neumeier, 2005) Existing frameworks describe brands as identities, perceptions, symbolic systems, or emotional associations, but they offer limited explanation of how internal organizational intention transforms into the emotional responses consumers carry with them. (Damasio, 1994; Kahneman, 2011) This paper introduces the Bigi Model, a mindset-driven framework that redefines the brand as an internal organizational stance that precedes behaviour, experience, and ultimately emotional meaning. Drawing on integrative theory building, the model synthesizes insights from classical branding theory, affective neuroscience, consumer decision science, and organizational culture research. The model proposes a four-stage pathway-mindset → behaviour → experience → feeling-and argues that visual identity elements such as logos, colours, and slogans operate merely as translators of the underlying mindset rather than as the brand itself. The study contributes to branding scholarship in three ways. First, it positions mindset as the conceptual origin of brand meaning. Second, it bridges the long-standing divide between internal organizational drivers and consumer emotional outcomes. Third, it offers a practical framework for managers seeking to build non-imitable, emotionally resonant brands in increasingly competitive markets. The Bigi Model provides a foundation for future empirical research on internal brand alignment, emotional consistency, and the measurement of brand mindset across cultures.

title: A Test of Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts
affiliations: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) - CUHK Business School, CUHK Business School, The Chinese University of Hong Kong and

detail.title: A Test of Lookahead Bias in LLM Forecasts
detail.abstract: We develop a statistical test to detect lookahead bias in economic forecasts generated by large language models (LLMs). Using state‑of‑the‑art pre‑training data detection techniques, we estimate the likelihood that a given prompt appeared in an LLM's training corpus, a statistic we term Lookahead Propensity (LAP). We formally show that a positive correlation between LAP and forecast accuracy indicates the presence and magnitude of lookahead bias, and apply the test to two forecasting tasks: news headlines predicting stock returns and earnings call transcripts predicting capital expenditures. Our test provides a cost-efficient, diagnostic tool for assessing the validity and reliability of LLM-generated forecasts.

title: Online shopping for a sustainable future: the mediating role of sustainable purchase intention in consumer decision-making
affiliations: Kashmir University, University  of Kashmir, Lovely Professional University and Govt. College for Women Nawakadal

detail.title: Online shopping for a sustainable future: the mediating role of sustainable purchase intention in consumer decision-making
detail.abstract:
This study analyzes the influence of environmental awareness, knowledge and attitude on sustainable purchase intention (SPI) and subsequent sustainable purchase decisions (SPD) within the setting of online shopping. It aims to explore how SPI functions as a mediating mechanism in this relationship.

A quantitative research design using a structured questionnaire was used to examine the influence of environmental awareness, knowledge and attitude on SPI and sustainable purchase decision. The survey was conducted offline in Jammu and Kashmir, India, to 357 consumers who had prior online shopping experience, who were selected through purposive sampling. To reduce response bias, participation was anonymous and voluntary, with screening questions ensuring relevant experience. The proposed model was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM).

The findings indicate that environmental knowledge, attitudes, and awareness significantly impact SPIs, which in turn mediates the relationship between these factors and sustainable purchase decisions. SPIs play a critical role in converting environmental concerns into actionable purchase decisions, bridging the gap between concerns and purchase tendencies.

The study offers insights for marketers, policymakers and e-commerce platforms by highlighting the importance of enhancing consumer awareness, knowledge and attitudes to strengthen intention and encourage purchase tendencies for sustainable goods and services in the online environment, thereby fostering sustainable consumerism and supporting sustainable purchasing behavior.

This research proposes a comprehensive conceptual framework in which SPI is studied as a mediator between environmental factors (knowledge, awareness and attitude) and sustainable purchase decision (SPD) in the context of online shopping. Unlike previous studies that have primarily examined these environmental concerns in isolation, this study simultaneously explores their combined influence, providing a more integrated and complete understanding of the drivers of sustainable online purchasing behavior. While the mediating role of SPI has been discussed in theories such as the theory of planned behavior (TPB) and value-belief-norm (VBN) theory, its application within the online shopping environment remains limited. By addressing this gap, the study contributes valuable insights for online marketers, businesses and policymakers aiming to promote sustainable consumer behavior.

detail.title: The Influence of Social Media Advertising on Purchase Intention among College Students

publicationDetails.detailsText: No,  this paper has not appeared, or been accepted to appear, in a Paper Series, Journal or Book.

detail.abstract: Social media advertising has transformed the digital marketing landscape and has become a key channel through which brands communicate with young consumers. Despite high levels of engagement, however, how social media advertising actually impacts the purchase behaviour of college students remains unclear, including debates about the mediating role of trust. This paper examines the impact that social media advertisements have on the buying intentions of college students. A quantitative research design was used, in which a structured questionnaire adapted from the validated scale of Sriram et al. (2021) was used. Responses were sought from 136 college students through the convenience sampling method. This study measured three key variables: trust, celebrity influence, and buying intention. Descriptive Statistics, Pearson's Correlation, Independent Sample t-tests, and One-Way ANOVA were used to analyse the data. The results showed that trust in advertising and purchase intention is positively correlated at 0.74, signifying that credibility is the number one driver for consumer action. Nevertheless, the test revealed no significant difference in the intention to buy based on past purchase behaviour, p > 0.05, or the type of social media platform, p > 0.05. These results show that for college students, the credibility of the advertisement supersedes platform loyalty or previous shopping habits, thus underlining the need for marketers to ensure authenticity.

title: Anthropology of Post-Growth Societies: Ritual, Value, Moral Economies, and Civilizational Transitions
affiliations: African Research Network (ARN)

detail.title: Anthropology of Post-Growth Societies: Ritual, Value, Moral Economies, and Civilizational Transitions
detail.abstract: As societies confront the ecological, economic, and ethical limits of GDP-centric growth, anthropological approaches provide critical insight into post-growth transformations. This paper explores the anthropology of post-GDP societies, emphasizing the role of ritual, moral economies, and value regimes in shaping collective well-being and civilizational trajectories. Drawing on comparative analyses from Africa, the Americas, and Asia, and engaging with recent scholarship (Graeber, Mbembe, Fischer, Comaroff & Comaroff), it examines how ritualized economies produce meaning, how moral economies sustain social cohesion, and how emerging value regimes catalyze civilizational transitions. The Kinshasa case study highlights relational economies and informal systems, illustrating post-growth practices in urban Africa. This framework offers a comparative lens for understanding the futures of the Global South, foregrounding anthropology as an essential tool for rethinking value, sustainability, and ethical development in the twenty-first century.

title: Navigating Manufacturer Encroachment in Live-Streaming E-Commerce Supply Chains
affiliations: South China University of Technology - School of Business Administration (SBA), Beijing Institute of Technology, University of Southampton and Hong Kong Polytechnic University

detail.title: Navigating Manufacturer Encroachment in Live-Streaming E-Commerce Supply Chains
detail.abstract: The rise of live-streaming commerce enables manufacturers to directly engage customers, challenging the traditional dominance of e-tailers and reshaping channel competition. This study examines a critical strategic question: whether, and under what conditions, manufacturers should encroach upon downstream markets through live-streaming channels. We develop a game-theoretic model involving a manufacturer, an e-tailer, and customers, analyzing three scenarios: a benchmark where only the e-tailer operates a live-streaming channel, manufacturer encroachment via a conventional direct channel, and manufacturer encroachment via its own live-streaming channel. Our analysis reveals that manufacturers always benefit from encroachment due to higher wholesale prices and direct sales revenues. However, manufacturers should adopt live-streaming only when return rates are sufficiently low and network externalities are sufficiently strong; otherwise, increased return costs outweigh the demand-expansion benefits of live-streaming. Interestingly, encroachment does not necessarily harm the e-tailer; under certain conditions, it can even enhance e-tailer profits by alleviating return losses via wholesale price adjustments. Moreover, we identify a "win-win" region where live-streaming encroachment boosts profits for both parties. This study provides actionable insights for manufacturers' channel strategies, underscoring the importance of managing return risks and leveraging network externalities for sustained competitive advantage.

title: The Strategic Role and Implications of User-Generated Content (UGC) in Contemporary Digital Branding

detail.title: The Strategic Role and Implications of User-Generated Content (UGC) in Contemporary Digital Branding
detail.abstract: This special report examines user-generated content (UGC) as a strategic branding instrument within the digital landscape. The relevance of the research stems from accelerated economic digitalization and a crisis of consumer trust in traditional advertising, necessitating novel approaches to brand development. Its scientific novelty consists in a comprehensive investigation of UGC's evolution from a tactical marketing tool into a systemic component of business models, facilitated by the construction of managed digital ecosystems. Through a comparative analysis of international and Russian cases, the study yields new findings demonstrating that integrating UGC into a strategic core enables the formation of stable communities of loyal consumers. Particular focus is placed on the mechanisms for embedding UGC into brand strategy via digital ecosystems, where content authenticity functions as a new currency of trust.

title: A Measure-Theoretic and Semimartingale Treatment of Linear Versus Compounded Returns
affiliations: Artificial Intelligence in Finance Institute

detail.title: A Measure-Theoretic and Semimartingale Treatment of Linear Versus Compounded Returns
detail.abstract: We develop a rigorous comparison between linear (simple) returns and compounded (logarithmic) returns in discrete and continuous time. Starting from a measure-theoretic foundation, we analyze the nonlinear transformation R → log(1 + R) as a map between L p spaces, characterize the Jensen gap via exact integral representations and cumulant expansions using Bell polynomials, and connect log returns to subadditive ergodic theorems and long-run growth rates. In continuous time, we interpret log returns via the Doléans-Dade stochastic exponential and relate instantaneous linear and log return rates through quadratic variation. We develop the theory of numéraire portfolios and growth-optimal strategies, analyze leverage effects and volatility feedback, examine portfolio aggregation, and discuss realized variance estimation with microstructure noise corrections following Barndorff-Nielsen and Shephard. Throughout, we emphasize the incompatibility between mean-variance preferences and growth-optimal (log-utility) criteria.

detail.abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence and nanotechnology can be integrated to develop autonomous drug delivery systems capable of improving therapeutic precision, real-time monitoring, and patient outcomes. Through a synthesis of emerging research, the paper highlights how AI-driven nanocarriers can independently sense biochemical signals, adapt to physiological changes, and release drugs with minimal human intervention. Findings show that despite major advancements, challenges such as biocompatibility, data processing stability, and regulatory uncertainty remain. The study concludes that integrating nanotechnology with AI offers transformative potential for personalized medicine, provided current limitations are strategically addressed.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management: A Comprehensive Framework for Organizational Implementation

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management: A Comprehensive Framework for Organizational Implementation
detail.abstract: The rapid proliferation of artificial intelligence technologies across organizational contexts has generated unprecedented opportunities alongside substantial risks that demand systematic management approaches. This article presents a comprehensive analysis of AI-related risks and develops an integrated framework for organizational risk management. Drawing upon interdisciplinary scholarship spanning computer science, management, law, and ethics, the analysis identifies and categorizes the multifaceted risks associated with AI deployment, including technical risks such as algorithmic bias, opacity, and security vulnerabilities; organizational risks encompassing operational disruptions, strategic misalignment, and governance challenges; and broader societal risks involving ethical concerns, systemic effects, and environmental impacts. The article critically examines existing governance frameworks at international, national, and organizational levels, evaluating their effectiveness in addressing the distinctive characteristics of AI systems. Furthermore, it proposes evidence-based mitigation strategies that organizations can implement across the AI lifecycle, from conception through deployment and ongoing operation. The framework emphasizes the importance of contextual adaptation, recognizing that effective AI risk management must account for sector-specific considerations, organizational maturity, and stakeholder expectations. By synthesizing theoretical insights with practical guidance, this article contributes to the growing body of knowledge supporting responsible AI adoption while enabling organizations to realize the transformative potential of these technologies.

title: Leveraging Social Learning for Agricultural Technology Adoption: Experimental Evidence from Kenya
affiliations: CIMMYT Kenya, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, CIMMYT Kenya, University of Sussex, International Maize And Wheat Improvement Center (CIMMYT), CIMMYT Kenya, International Maize and Wheat Improvement Centre and International Maize and Wheat Improvement Centre

detail.title: Leveraging Social Learning for Agricultural Technology Adoption: Experimental Evidence from Kenya

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflict or interest to declare

detail.abstract: Farmer experimentation is fundamental to agricultural technology adoption. Yet, onfarm experimentation in rural Africa is often uncoordinated, invisible, and limited in scope, reducing the scope for social learning. We conducted a randomized controlled trial in Kenya to assess the impact of increased coordination, visibility and scale of experimentation. All treatment arms improved coordination by providing selected maize seed to randomly selected host farmers along with signage and instructions. One treatment arm further rewarded hosts financially, and another treatment arm increased the number of hosts reached. Using panel data among experimenting hosts and other non-host village farmers, we document the impact of these interventions on beliefs, demand and adoption of hybrid maize. All treatment arms increased awareness and demand. The incentives arm most boosts hosts' efforts to disseminate (and resulted in strong learning and demand for the hosts). Yet, it's an increase in the number of hosts (scale) which resulted in stronger learning and demand effects for non-hosts. This indicates a dual-learning mechanism: incentives enhance signal precision, while saturation facilitates match quality in heterogeneous learning environments and, hence, reach. All treatments struggled to increase adoption substantially, due to supply constraints.

detail.abstract: The Elevator Safety Equipment Market represents a critical intersection between urban infrastructure development, regulatory enforcement, and technological innovation. title: The Persistence of External Pressures and Domestic Fiscal Strain: An Analysis of Kenyan Macroeconomic Indicators (Q4 2025)

detail.title: The Persistence of External Pressures and Domestic Fiscal Strain: An Analysis of Kenyan Macroeconomic Indicators (Q4 2025)
detail.abstract: This paper analyses key macroeconomic indicators for the Kenyan economy as of early December 2025, drawing on data from the Central Bank of Kenya's Weekly Bulletin. We observe a continued easing of headline and core inflation, juxtaposed with persistent exchange rate volatility and elevated domestic and external public debt. The money market remains liquid, with stable interbank rates (KESONIA at 9.25%), reflecting effective monetary policy steering. However, robust demand for government securities at high average interest rates underscores the market's perception of sovereign risk and the government's high domestic borrowing requirement. We conclude that while disinflationary forces are taking hold, long-term fiscal sustainability and external balance remain the primary challenges to Kenya's mediumterm economic outlook.

title: Cultural Distance Labor Penalty: Cultural Distance is Associated with Migrant Employment Gaps Across Europe
affiliations: London School of Economics, London School of Economics, London School of Economics and London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE)

detail.title: Cultural Distance Labor Penalty: Cultural Distance is Associated with Migrant Employment Gaps Across Europe
detail.abstract: Migrant labor force participation varies by migrant characteristics. Using the Eurostat Labour Force Survey, we analyze employment gaps between migrants and native-born workers across 16 European host countries and 128 migrant home countries. We regress the migrant–native employment gap on cultural distance while controlling for education, population size, GDP per capita, migrant population size, genetic distance, and home-country fixed effects. In pooled models, a one standard deviation increase in cultural distance is associated with a 1.97 percentage point increase in the migrant employment gap. To assess robustness, we conduct a multiverse analysis across all reasonable model specifications. Across 887 home-host pairs, greater cultural distance is positively associated with larger employment gaps in 355 of 384 specifications. The fully specified model explains 57% of the variance. Cultural distance accounts for the largest share of explained variance in pooled and sex-disaggregated models, with additive conditional R² values of .127 (pooled), .081 (male), and .167 (female). Results are robust to leave-one-cluster-out analyses, alternative loss functions, controls for host-country unemployment, outlier removal, alternative imputation methods, and varying migrant population thresholds. The cultural distance penalty is larger for female migrants than for males and varies across host countries. More inclusive integration policies, measured by the Migrant Integration Policy Index (MIPEX), are associated with a larger cultural distance penalty, revealing a “migrant policy paradox”. Lower employment gaps are also associated with higher home-country education, population size, GDP per capita, and greater genetic distance, while larger co-national migrant populations are associated with higher gaps. Although the causal mechanism remains unclear, the results are consistent with cultural barriers to economic integration.

title: Group Identity and Strategic Games in the Laboratory
affiliations: ESADE Business School and

detail.title: Group Identity and Strategic Games in the Laboratory
detail.abstract: We study the effects of group identity on cooperation in experimental strategic games. Our results show that in games of strategic complements, group identity only matters initially when a participant interacts with another participant of the same group identity by delivering more cooperative choices, but this effect disappears after a few interactions. However, in treatments with strategic substitutes, we find that participants are persistently less cooperative when playing with another participant of a different group. We show that these effects arise through differences in social preferences and learning dynamics. In games with strategic substitutes, out-group participants display spiteful preferences and tend to imitate the most successful opponent, whereas in games with strategic complements, behavior aligns with standard preferences and is consistent with fictitious play learning.

title: Prison, Probation, and the Community
affiliations: University of St. Gallen

detail.title: Prison, Probation, and the Community
detail.abstract: This paper examines how incarceration and probation shape community crime rates with 20 years of administrative court records from Milwaukee, Wisconsin. I estimate causal effects by instrumenting for a criminal defendant's sentence with the preferences of a randomly assigned judge. I extend the canonical randomized judge design framework to incorporate effects generated along the intensive margin of sentence durations. This framework allows me to distinguish between effects to the marginally incarcerated defendant from effects to non-marginal defendants. Empirically, I find that longer sentences reduce defendant recidivism for both probation and incarceration. For the marginal defendant, this may lead to offsetting dynamics on the margin of incarceration. At the neighborhood level, however, only incarceration generates crime-reducing spillover effects in nearby households. I provide evidence that these effects are driven by the incapacitation of high severity offenders.

title: What Do Large Factor Models Learn? Self-Induced Regularization, Cost of Overfitting, and Self-Adaptivity

detail.title: What Do Large Factor Models Learn? Self-Induced Regularization, Cost of Overfitting, and Self-Adaptivity
detail.abstract: This paper studies the out-of-sample performance of large, overparameterized linear factor models for stochastic discount factor (SDF) estimation. Motivated by recent advances in finance and machine learning, we analyze the all-inclusive ridge estimator that incorporates all candidate factors without ex-ante screening or dimension reduction. Our new non-asymptotic pricing error bounds reveal that including many low-variance principal components implicitly increases the effective penalty on high-variance components, shrinking the estimated SDF and biasing performance. We further show that exact interpolation in the low-variance space leads to bounded out-of-sample deterioration, as the fitted coefficients behave effectively like zero and incur little additional error relative to underspecification. In addition, ridge regression self-adapts by emphasizing top principal components without knowing which factors are important, effectively mimicking a data-driven cutoff in principal component regression. These findings extend benign overfitting theory to the inherently misspecified setting of SDF estimation, where classical linear regression assumptions fail. Empirically, we validate these insights using U.S. equity data and large factor sets constructed via Random Fourier Features (RFF). We find that noise factors degrade performance through bias rather than variance inflation, and that adding weak but priced factors can hurt model performance. Lastly, we show that mildly negative ridge penalties can enhance model performance, consistent with our theoretical prediction that they partially offset self-induced regularization.

detail.abstract: There is an old adage emphasizing ‘necessity is the mother of invention’.  Innovation requires coming out of the comfort zone.  Transformation is painful and generally is meted out with resistance.  It requires a vision, resolve, and perseverance to ‘transform, perform, and reform’.  Pandemic exposed nationalities to the greater challenges of overreliance on international markets for basic requirements of a nation.  When the borders were shut for trade, one had to look inward for the basic requirements like masks and vaccines.  Over-reliance on international trade for economic growth exposed the severe challenge of uncertainties not only with reference to climate change but also because of geopolitical situations (like Russia-Ukraine war).  It was then the Prime Minister of India announced (on 12th May, 2020) ‘the Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan’, an economic package of Rs. 20 lakh crores (approx. $306 bn USD), to boost various sectors of the economy, in particular catering to the demography and demand by improving infrastructure and systems.  Aatmanirbhar Bharat has been a measure necessitated because of pandemic, however, it has boosted the 2014 initiative of ‘Make in India’ as well.  In all this, focus of making in India and becoming self-reliant, India’s commitment to international trade and policy including the regime of non-discrimination cannot be lost sight of.  The mantra of providing an ecosystem of fair competition to the businesses around the world shall be sustained.  As said by Hon’ble Prime Minister, “When India speaks of becoming self-reliant, it doesn't advocate a self-centred system. In India's self-reliance; there is a concern for the whole world's happiness, cooperation and peace”.  This becomes more so important when India is emerging as a world leader and hope for many countries to ensure peace and sustainability.  India’s commitment at Glasgow (COP26) for achieving net zero would require support from the whole world, however, at the same time, focus on self-reliance can only cut the carbon emissions, movement towards renewable energy shedding fossil fuels.  While doing so, India cannot lose sight of the global commitments under WTO, else it would lead to disputes like Solar Panel Subsidy cases, agricultural subsidy cases, etc.  The competition law of India does not differentiate between enterprises public or private.  Though competition law enforcement can only ensure competition in India, a robust national competition law and dispute resolution regime always provides hope to the business players around the world boosting ease of doing business (EODB).  Competition can only be with equals and competition law has to ensure that the smaller players are not crushed away, and it becomes a special responsibility of the larger players to allow space for them to grow.  This paper would analyse the concept of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and its interface with the competition law and policy and our international trade commitments at WTO.

title: Template Power: How Instruction Templates Redistribute Decision Rights
affiliations: Universidad de la Republica

detail.title: Template Power: How Instruction Templates Redistribute Decision Rights
detail.abstract: This article examines how instruction templates and system prompts function as a regla compilada that redistributes decision rights in downstream model outputs. Focusing on five institutional domains, we construct a controlled synthetic corpus of 1000 prompts, each executed under five template conditions, and quantify shifts in authority-bearing constructions across 5000 generated texts. A syntactic authority inventory operationalizes seven indicators, including delegation ratio, veto path count, default scope strength, agent deletion rate, deontic stack depth, escalation clause presence and override friction. Using intra-prompt comparisons and mixed-effects models, we estimate the causal impact of template variants on the locus of control, robustness of exceptions and balance between model-proposed and human-confirmed decisions. Robustness checks include template ablations, adversarial prompts and placebo reformulations to disentangle authority effects from style. The article delivers a Template Authority Index, a public test battery and a de-identified dataset to support external replication. The central claim is that seemingly minor changes in instruction templates produce systematic and measurable reallocations of authority in institutional texts, with direct implications for governance, accountability and the design of human–AI decision pipelines.

title: Natural Disaster Exposure and Climate Change Beliefs
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome, Sapienza University of Rome and Sapienza University of Rome

detail.title: Natural Disaster Exposure and Climate Change Beliefs
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how direct exposure to climate-related natural disasters shapes the evolution of climate change beliefs over time. Using survey data collected through face-to-face interviews in Italy, we analyze perceived climate change severity across three temporal horizons (past, present, and future), accounting for heterogeneity in individual characteristics. We first provide regression-based evidence on the relationship between disaster exposure and perceived severity. We then examine belief updating dynamics by estimating non-homogeneous Markov transition matrices conditional on individual traits. Our findings show that exposure to natural disasters is associated with higher climaterelated concern and greater persistence in high-severity belief states. Belief updating is heterogeneous: younger and risk-loving individuals tend to revise their perceptions more sharply following exposure, whereas older or risk-averse respondents display more gradual updating patterns.

title: The Social Determinants of Bank Runs

detail.title: The Social Determinants of Bank Runs
detail.abstract: Motivated by new evidence from the 2023 U.S. regional bank crisis, I develop a theory of how depositor social structure influences bank runs. Rumors about bank financial health spread via interpersonal communication, triggering withdrawals that may lead to  collapse. I show that the occurrence, speed, and scale of runs depend on depositor connectedness—the likelihood that agents know and communicate with each other. Higher connectedness accelerates information spread, making runs faster and more severe. In contrast, dispersed depositor bases slow down runs, and can even prevent them entirely.

title: A Python Integration of Practical Asset Allocation Based on Modern Portfolio Theory and Its Advancements

detail.title: A Python Integration of Practical Asset Allocation Based on Modern Portfolio Theory and Its Advancements

publicationDetails.detailsText: ZHAW School of Management and Law, Digital Collection, 2021 https://doi.org/10.21256/zhaw-24351

detail.abstract:
This thesis develops a Python-based implementation of practical asset allocation methods based on modern portfolio theory and its extensions. The mean-variance framework introduced by Markowitz remains the standard approach for investment decisions, yet publicly available software tools for portfolio optimization are scarce despite extensive academic research on improved methods.

We address this gap by engineering asset allocation tools in Python using convex optimization to formulate portfolio problems with various investment constraints. We extend the classical framework beyond the first two moments of return distributions by integrating expected shortfall to capture tail risk more effectively. To reduce estimation errors, we implement shrinkage estimators that combine sample covariance matrices with structured estimators and demonstrate improved out-of-sample performance. Each optimization problem is examined through analytical derivations and numerical examples, with code snippets and visualizations provided for reproducibility.

Empirical studies using Swiss equity market data show that portfolios constructed with our methods achieve competitive returns while exhibiting lower expected shortfall and reduced excess risk relative to benchmark indices in highly correlated market environments. Our results confirm that most portfolio optimization problems can be expressed in convex form and solved efficiently using Python, providing practitioners with a robust framework for real-world asset allocation.

title: Forecasting Equity Correlations with Hybrid Transformer Graph Neural Network
affiliations: , University of Queensland and Independent

detail.title: Forecasting Equity Correlations with Hybrid Transformer Graph Neural Network

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Paper originally developed by Jack Fanshawe (primary author) as thesis for Bachelor of Advanced Finance and Economics from the University of Queensland, Rumi Masih and Alexander Cameron served as thesis advises throughout the period.

detail.abstract: This paper studies forward-looking stock-stock correlation forecasting for S&P 500 constituents and evaluates whether learned correlation forecasts can improve graph-based clustering used in basket trading strategies. We cast 10-day ahead correlation prediction in Fisher-z space and train a Temporal-Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network (THGNN) to predict residual deviations from a rolling historical baseline. The architecture combines a Transformer-based temporal encoder, which captures non-stationary, complex, temporal dependencies, with an edge-aware graph attention network that propagates cross-asset information over the equity network. Inputs span daily returns, technicals, sector structure, previous correlations, and macro signals, enabling regime-aware forecasts and attention-based feature and neighbor importance to provide interpretability. Outof-sample results from 2019-2024 show that the proposed model meaningfully reduces correlation forecasting error relative to rolling-window estimates. When integrated into a graph-based clustering framework, forward-looking correlations produce adaptable and economically meaningfully baskets, particularly during periods of market stress. These findings suggest that improvements in correlation forecasts translate into meaningful gains during portfolio construction tasks.

title: Human-AI Handovers: A Dynamic Authority Reversal Framework for Trust Calibration and Transitional Accountability

detail.title: Human-AI Handovers: A Dynamic Authority Reversal Framework for Trust Calibration and Transitional Accountability
detail.abstract: Human-artificial intelligence collaboration is increasingly treated as a static allocation problem-humans decide, machines compute-yet high-stakes workflows reveal a more fluid reality: leadership shifts multiple times within a single decision episode. This paper formalizes the Dynamic Authority Reversal (DAR) framework, which models intra-episode authority transitions across four states: Human-Leader/AI-Follower (HL), AI-Leader/Human-Follower (AL), Co-Leadership (CO), and Mutual Override (MO). Transitions are governed by four trigger classes-data superiority, contextual judgment requirements, risk thresholds, and ethics overrides-and are stabilized through hysteresis bands and safe-exit timers. The framework couples micro-level trust calibration with macro-level legitimacy by introducing the Reversal Register, an auditable log that binds each decision to the prevailing authority state, trigger conditions, and justificatory explanations. Ten falsifiable propositions are derived and linked to measurement constructs, prioritized by foundational importance and empirical tractability. Sector-specific implementation guidance is provided for healthcare and public administration, with attention to existing governance structures and regulatory frameworks. By operationalizing handovers rather than merely prescribing "human oversight," DAR advances both theory and practice: it equips researchers with testable hypotheses, furnishes practitioners with governance-ready instruments, and offers regulators an auditable architecture that preserves ultimate human accountability while enabling reversible AI leadership where contextually advantageous.

detail.abstract: This study examines two recent tax reforms in Peru aimed at fostering economic growth. A Dynamic Computable General Equilibrium (DCGE) model calibrated with 2023 data is employed to evaluate their macroeconomic and sectoral impacts. The results show that the Municipal Compensation Fund Law generates limited aggregate effects, with some notable exceptions: it tends to reduce the value added of the construction sector while increasing public expenditure on goods and services. title: Revenue Generation in the Maritime industry, A Case of Ghana Maritime Authority

detail.title: Revenue Generation in the Maritime industry, A Case of Ghana Maritime Authority
detail.abstract: The study examined how the Ghana Maritime Authority generates and mobilizes revenue. The study specifically assessed the challenges affecting the effective generation and mobilization of revenue by the GMA. It developed strategies for the Ghana Maritime Authority to ensure effective operation and generation of revenue. The study was a descriptive, cross-sectional one and adopted a quantitative approach. 38 questionnaires with a reliability of 0.85 were distributed through personal contact and self-administration by the employees and management of GMA. The study found out that the revenue generation methods used by GMA were: fees of the various shipping lines, registration of ships, issuance of certificates to attest seaworthiness and compliance, survey and inspection of vessels, training of boat operators/mechanics, boat safety educational program, sale of discharge books to seafarers, certification and examination of seafarers, conducting of exams for seafarers, issuance of eligibility letters to applicants and issuance medical certificate to seafarers. On the contrary, the study found that the challenges confronted by GMA in their revenue mobilization were: inadequate logistics, inadequate professional personnel, inadequate infrastructure and equipment, inadequate legal provisions (laws and regulations), political interference, and improper administrative structures. Again, the extent to which GMA monitored the revenue mobilization process was somehow high; it was encouraging but not the best. The study advised that the management of GMA should put proper strategies, systems, and structures in place to identify other revenue sources.

detail.abstract: The rise of financial regulation in the private law domain raises intricate questions about the interplay between EU financial regulation and private law. What is the role of the public/private divide in EU financial regulation? How does the legal grammar of EU harmonisation measures influence the relationship between regulatory standards with a European origin and national private law norms, and the way such measures are enforced? And how should EU financial regulation and private law ultimately relate to each other? While significant scholarly attention has been devoted to the relationship between EU financial regulation and private law, this chapter revisits this relationship in the light of a new geopolitical reality characterised, in particular, by the unravelling of the post-World War II global order and the global surge of autocratic powers and anti-democratic forces that the EU should navigate. It argues that the immense challenges facing the EU require a more integrated approach to EU financial regulation and private law at both the EU and national levels.

title: Trading Electrons: Predicting DART Spread Spikes in ISO Electricity Markets
affiliations: Princeton University - Department of Operations Research and Financial Engineering, Princeton University and Princeton University

detail.title: Trading Electrons: Predicting DART Spread Spikes in ISO Electricity Markets
detail.abstract: We study the problem of forecasting and optimally trading day-ahead versus realtime (DART) price spreads in U.S. wholesale electricity markets. Building on the framework of [9], we extend spike prediction from a single zone to a multi-zone setting and treat both positive and negative DART spikes within a unified statistical model. To translate directional signals into economically meaningful positions, we develop a structural and market-consistent price impact model based on day-ahead bid stacks. This yields closed-form expressions for the optimal vector of zonal INC/DEC quantities, capturing asymmetric buy/sell impacts and cross-zone congestion effects. When applied to NYISO, the resulting impact-aware strategy significantly improves the risk-return profile relative to unit-size trading and highlights substantial heterogeneity across markets and seasons.

title: Pecking Order Revisited
affiliations: Case Western Reserve University - Department of Banking & Finance and Case Western Reserve University

detail.title: Pecking Order Revisited
detail.abstract: We examine the validity of pecking-order by examining the determinants of capital structure for S&P 500 firms for the recent 25 years from 2000 to 2024. We use traditional regression models and machine-learning approaches to examine how firm fundamentals and macroeconomic conditions shape firm capital structure. Across several methods including OLS, Lasso, Ridge, Random Forest, and Gradient Boosting regressions, three variables, on average, consistently and significantly explain leverage for a firm: operating profitability, tax-shield benefit, and earnings volatility. Profitable firms rely less on debt, aligning with the pecking-order prediction that internal funds are preferred when available. Firms with larger tax shields or greater earnings volatility prefer to borrow debt when there are tax advantages to doing so, and/or when internal funds are more uncertain. Non-linear models highlight liquidity also as a predictor of leverage, indicating that internal cash buffer reduces the need for external financing. Among macro variables, GDP growth is associated with lower leverage, reflecting deleveraging during expansions.

title: A Decision Support Framework for Analytical Optimisation in Clinical Coding

detail.title: A Decision Support Framework for Analytical Optimisation in Clinical Coding
detail.abstract: This study presents a mathematical model supported by artificial intelligence and decision-support algorithms to optimise the hospital clinical coding process, which involves translating information from electronic health records into standardised diagnosis and procedure codes. The proposed model incorporates heuristic rules, automated data processing, and real-time validation mechanisms and is structured around defining the coding system, classifying clinical episodes by entity, estimating hospital-level staffing needs, and organising a scalable application framework that relies on centralised, anonymised health data to ensure adaptability across healthcare systems. To evaluate the approach, a simulation using retrospective data from 43 hospital entities between 2019 and 2024 was conducted and compared with current practices and the experimental model, with a prospective operational analysis planned for 2025 to 2027. The modelling showed a moderate difference between simulated and actual hospital data (median KS D ≈ 0.209). It revealed substantial asymmetry in episode distribution, as roughly half of the smaller hospital units accounted for only 15 to 20 percent of total episodes, while the top 25 percent generated more than 60 percent of total activity. Further assessment of operational flow and demand coverage capacity indicated a systemic and predictable failure of the existing capacity model for 2025 to 2027. In contrast, the experimental model produced significant improvements in process efficiency. Overall, the results demonstrate that integrating AI and coding-support mechanisms can reduce coding time, strengthen communication among coding professionals, improve human resource allocation, promote standardisation and equity across hospitals, and likely reduce associated costs, all while enhancing rather than replacing the role of human coders. Although the model is built on the Portuguese healthcare context, it can be adapted and applied to other healthcare systems.

title: The Effects of Place-Based Startup Policy Mix on Local Entrepreneurship: Evidence from City Government Survey in Japan
affiliations: and

detail.title: The Effects of Place-Based Startup Policy Mix on Local Entrepreneurship: Evidence from City Government Survey in Japan

declarations.funderStatement: The study for this paper is a part of Kakenhi Basic Research B Project No. 20H01491 by Japan Society for the Promotion of Science (JSPS).

detail.abstract: Place-based economic policies have attracted research attention. Previous studies have discussed the advantages of local governments due to the heterogeneity of local conditions and environment. In recent years, most Japanese cities have provided various types of startup support for various types of potential founders and startups for regional revitalization. However, no empirical studies have addressed local startup support by considering and comparing different types of startup support. Based on our original survey data of Japanese cities, we fill these gaps by estimating the effects of city-level startup support on local startup activities by comparing different support measures. Using a city-level panel dataset with seven periods over 20 years and panel fixed effect models, we find that both hard support (subsidies) and soft support (seminars) have positive and significant effects on the number of new establishments, whereas subsidies reduce the average size of new firms, suggesting a trade-off between policy goals.

title: Contributions of the Study to the Ghana Maritime Authority, the Maritime Industry in Ghana, and West Africa

detail.title: Contributions of the Study to the Ghana Maritime Authority, the Maritime Industry in Ghana, and West Africa
detail.abstract: Contributions of the Study to the Ghana Maritime Authority, the Maritime Industry in Ghana, and West Africa This study on revenue generation and mobilization by the Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) offers critical insights and practical recommendations that contribute significantly to the enhancement of the GMA's operations, the maritime industry in Ghana, and the broader West African sub-region. Contributions to Ghana Maritime Authority (GMA) Improved Revenue Generation Strategies: The study identifies various revenue generation methods successfully employed by GMA, such as fees and charges on shipping lines, ship registration, issuance of compliance certificates, surveys and inspections, and training and certification of seafarers. Importantly, it highlights areas with the highest revenue contribution and those with potential for improvement, enabling the GMA to allocate resources efficiently and refine its revenue streams. Identification of Inhibiting Factors: Crucial challenges such as inadequate logistics, political interference, inadequate infrastructure, and weak legal frameworks have been diagnosed as factors impeding effective revenue mobilization. Recognizing these obstacles allows the GMA to prioritize addressing these issues, advocate for better legal provisions, and improve logistics and infrastructure to enhance operational capacity. Enhanced Monitoring and Control Mechanisms: The assessment of existing monitoring systems reveals that GMA has established computerized support, regular simulation analyses, and internal audits. The study encourages strengthening these mechanisms, particularly cash flow monitoring, to ensure continuous efficiency in revenue collection and financial accountability. Recommendations for Capacity Building and Governance: By recommending staff training, clearer administrative structures, reduction of political interference, and the creation of a marine think tank drawing on maritime sector expertise (taking cues from successful models like Singapore's maritime administration), the study provides GMA management with actionable strategies to enhance professionalism, governance, and strategic development capacity.

title: Dividend Discount Model and Catering Theory Revisited
affiliations: Case Western Reserve University - Department of Banking & Finance and Case Western Reserve University

detail.abstract: We examine the determinants of divided payout policy, measured using three measures: the dividend-to-net-income ratio, shares repurchased-to-net-income ratio, and the dividend plus repurchases-to-net-income ratio. Two groups of explanatory variables are considered. The first group consists of firm characteristics (including lagged ones), and the second group comprises macroeconomic indicators reflecting economic conditions. Across OLS, Random Forest, Ridge and Lasso methodologies, as well as in univariate tests, the price to earnings (P/E) ratio consistently and significantly shows a positive contemporaneous association with payout intensity, consistent with the simple dividend discount model, and, to a lesser extent, the catering theory (Baker & Wurgler, 2004).

title: Virtue, Telos, and the Future of Doctoring in an Age of Artificial Intelligence

detail.title: Virtue, Telos, and the Future of Doctoring in an Age of Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this work.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), defined here as computational technologies such as machine learning algorithms, large language models, and predictive analytics platforms capable of complex cognitive tasks like human reasoning, is fundamentally reshaping medical practice. While these systems can increase diagnostic accuracy and efficiency by synthesizing vast data, they also introduce ethical complexities that challenge the moral, interpersonal, and purposedriven dimensions central to the physician's role. Some proponents argue that AI could enhance empathy and patient-centeredness by automating routine tasks, allowing physicians more time to focus on patient interaction. However, virtue ethics remains essential, as the nuances of human judgment, empathy, and moral discernment cannot be replicated by machines. 'Telos' here means the ultimate goal of medicine, and 'phronesis' denotes practical wisdom—the ability to make prudent decisions in specific situations. Drawing on philosophical frameworks from Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, Thomas Aquinas's Summa Theologiae, and Dr. Edmund D. Pellegrino's normative analyses, this article develops a forward-looking paradigm for medicine that maintains the centrality of human judgment, virtue, and the patient-physician relationship. Integrating virtue ethics and contemporary bioethics, I argue that physicians must pair technological expertise with moral discernment. Central is a renewed commitment to medicine's telos—the holistic good of the patient—and deliberate cultivation of phronesis. Thus, I advocate frameworks in education, ethics, and system design to ensure that AI remains a tool, not a substitute, for human moral agency.

title: The Judicial Sentinel: Navigating the Nexus of National Courts and International Commercial Arbitration
affiliations: Senior Judicial Magistrate at Bangladesh Judicial Service

detail.abstract: The Judicial Sentinel, by Judge Nazmul Hasan (11th BJS), is a definitive jurist-led guide for aligning domestic judicial practice with global arbitration standards. It masterfully navigates the "Supportive Hand" of national courts—from enforcing arbitration clauses to the cross-border recognition of awards—offering an essential roadmap for judges and practitioners to foster investor-friendly legal environments and uphold the Rule of Law in a borderless commercial world.

title: Policy Entrepreneurship in a "Thawing" Authoritarian Context: Exploring the Narratives from Participatory Budgeting Reform
affiliations: KDI School of Public Policy and Management

detail.title: Policy Entrepreneurship in a "Thawing" Authoritarian Context: Exploring the Narratives from Participatory Budgeting Reform

publicationDetails.detailsText: KDI School of Pub Policy & Management Paper No. DS2-07
publicationDetails.journalName: KDI School of Public Policy & Management Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Policy entrepreneurship is extensively studied in developed contexts, both focusing on select countries and from a comparative approach. However, how and which policy entrepreneurs engage at different stages of the policy process in authoritarian contexts, often under the conditions of regime uncertainty, is an understudied theme. Yet, during the times of political openings, or regime thawing, a window of opportunity arises for policy entrepreneurs to selectively engage with the means vs. the ends of government reforms. Entrepreneurial opportunities may be shaped by the authoritarian context where actors external to government entities will have limited openings for participation, however. The narratives that emerge from our interviews with public officials show that the participatory budgeting reform in Uzbekistan is incomplete in two key aspects. First, it focuses almost exclusively on the means vs. the ends of participatory budgeting. Second, the role and engagement of external stakeholders, such as civic groups and citizenry, are found to be limited beyond access points defined by the government. For participatory reform process to be complete, the shortcomings must be remedied in what could become a "participatory budget reform" 2.0.

title: The 3 Cultures of One's Cultural Code

detail.title: The 3 Cultures of One's Cultural Code
