detail.abstract: This chapter examines the role of collective labour rights in regulating artificial intelligence (AI) at work within EU labour law. Starting from the premise that collective rights constitute a core pillar of workplace governance, it explores how the introduction of AI challenges both the purpose and the effectiveness of existing industrial-relations frameworks. The chapter shows how AI intensifies longstanding tensions between emancipatory and managerial conceptions of collective rights, while simultaneously reshaping power dynamics within and beyond the employment relationship. After mapping the main channels through which collective actors engage in workplace governance, the chapter proposes a taxonomy of AI systems based on their underlying empowerment dynamics, distinguishing between algorithmic management, capabilityenhancing tools, and AI systems that emulate or replace human labour. Building on this framework, it identifies significant gaps in the current regulatory and bargaining landscape, including the reduction of collective rights to transparency obligations and the exclusion of technology-controlling actors from labour governance. The chapter concludes by calling for a recalibration of collective labour rights to ensure meaningful worker participation in AI governance at work.

detail.title: Beyond Survival: Nonprofit Organizational Adaptation in the Shadow of Success
detail.abstract: This article develops a conceptual framework for understanding how nonprofit organizations navigate the “success paradox”, the phenomenon whereby achieving organizational goals paradoxically threatens organizational survival. Drawing on organizational theories of adaptation, resource dependence and institutional isomorphism, we argue that success operates as an exogenous condition that fundamentally reshapes the political and economic environment in which nonprofit organizations operate. The article advances nonprofit management scholarship by offering eleven distinct adaptive pathways organizations may pursue when confronting success, organized into three categories: non-adaptive strategies, strategic adaptive responses, and perverse strategies. It further examines how structural constraints, particularly political opportunity structures and resource dependencies, limit which pathways remain viable. We demonstrate that the success paradox reveals fundamental tensions between effective issue advocacy and sustainable nonprofit development, challenging conventional understandings of organizational effectiveness.

title: Team Disagreement and Productive Persuasion

detail.title: Team Disagreement and Productive Persuasion
detail.abstract: We study how open disagreement influences team performance in a dynamic production game. Team members can hold different priors about the productivity of the available production technologies. Initial beliefs are common knowledge and updated based on observed production outcomes. We show that when only one technology is available, a player works harder early on when her coworkers are initially more pessimistic about the technology's productivity. Holding average team optimism constant, this force implies that a team's expected output increases in the degree of disagreement of its members. A manager with the task of forming two-member teams from a large workforce maximizes total expected output by matching coworkers' beliefs in a negative assortative way. When alternative, equally good, production technologies are available, a disagreeing team outperforms any like-minded team in terms of average output and team members' welfare.

detail.title: Energy-Aware Integrated Order Assignment and Routing for Heterogeneous Couriers in on-Demand Delivery
detail.abstract: On-demand delivery (ODD) platforms increasingly rely on heterogeneous courier workforces (in-house, supplementary dedicated, and crowdsourced couriers) to meet stringent time-window requirements. Among these types, crowdsourced couriers—the workforce backbone—predominantly utilize battery-swapping two-wheeled electric vehicles (TWEVs) to sustain high-frequency operations. In the face of these evolving characteristics, however, operational practices at our industrial partner, JD.com, reveal a critical gap: current dispatching systems often manage resources in silos and overlook energy-logistics couplings, specifically energy-constrained order assignments, speed variations dependent on state of charge (SoC) and mandatory detours for battery swapping. This oversight frequently leads to unexecutable plans and delivery delays. To address this, we propose an energy-aware integrated order assignment and routing model that unifies the dispatching of diverse courier types while explicitly capturing non-linear energy constraints and battery swapping operations. To solve this computationally challenging problem, we design a nested tabu search algorithm based on a dual-level ``fast search–precise evaluation" structure. The outer level conducts fast global assignment search with an incremental routing heuristic, while the inner level incrementally solves courier-level exact routing subproblems to ensure accurate cost evaluation. Extensive experiments using real-world data demonstrate that our algorithm yields high-quality solutions efficiently. Crucially, the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional dispatching strategies that neglect energy dynamics. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses provide managerial insights into how the increased number of swap cabinets, expanded crowdsourced capacity, improved battery efficiency and capacity can enhance system efficiency and mitigate courier fatigue. Overall, this study paves the way for sustainable and reliable urban delivery systems.

title: Mapping excess housing demand using big search data

detail.title: Mapping excess housing demand using big search data
detail.abstract: Tackling the housing affordability crisis is a priority for policymakers worldwide, yet decisions about where to build new homes are rarely informed by direct measures of local housing demand. Using novel data on over 10 billion housing searches from Great Britain's largest online property portal between 2019 and 2024, we construct a new micro-neighbourhood measure of excess demand-the housing gap. The housing gap captures households' unconstrained location preferences, revealing where demand exceeds supply. We find that excess demand is highest in both high-and low-price neighbourhoods with attractive amenities and fast employment access, such as inner cities and large towns, and lowest in areas with local disamenities and rural locations. Furthermore, a significant portion of variation in the housing gap occurs within rather than between local authorities, highlighting the limitations of broad-based housing targets. We visualise these patterns in an interactive online mapping tool designed to inform housing policy.

detail.abstract: There is a general concern that present developments in artificial intelligence (AI) research will lead to sentient AI systems, and these may pose an existential threat to humanity. But why cannot sentient AI systems benefit humanity instead? This paper endeavours to put this question in a tractable manner. I ask whether a putative AI system will develop an altruistic or a malicious disposition towards our society, or what would be the nature of its agency? Given that AI systems are being developed into formidable problem solvers, we can reasonably expect these systems to preferentially take on conscious aspects of human problem solving. I identify the relevant phenomenal aspects of agency in human problem solving. The functional aspects of conscious agency can be monitored using tools provided by functionalist theories of consciousness. A recent expert report (Butlin et al. 2023) has identified functionalist indicators of agency based on these theories. I show how to use the Integrated Information Theory (IIT) of consciousness, to monitor the phenomenal nature of this agency. If we are able to monitor the agency of AI systems as they develop, then we can dissuade them from becoming a menace to society while encouraging them to be an aid.

detail.abstract: How are emancipatory alternatives enacted and sustained within existing social arrangements? Drawing on Erik Olin Wright’s concept of real utopias, this paper examines the organizational pathways through which interstitial social change is cultivated. Empirically, the study draws on comparative ethnographic research with three citizens’ movement organizations in South Korea engaging in education for democracy. Based on fifteen months of participant observation, interviews, and document analysis, the paper shows how activist-educators design educational practices and organizational arrangements that mediate between individual transformation and broader societal change. Across cases, pedagogical third spaces are produced through three organizational pathways: 1) internal buffering within a social movement organization, 2) intermediary infrastructuring between civil society and the state, and 3) distributed coordination across networked organizations. The findings highlight organizations not simply as sites where liminal experiences occur, but as active producers of liminality through the intentional design of pedagogical practices, organizational arrangements, and discursive resources. I conceptualize these arrangements as pedagogical third spaces: organizationally embedded, in-between spaces that mediate individual transformation and broader societal change. By foregrounding how activist-educators cultivate and sustain such spaces, the paper shifts attention from liminality as an episodic condition to liminality as an organizational process—one that enables collective agency to develop beyond formal organizational boundaries.

detail.title: The Post-Brown Era in Judicial Policymaking
detail.abstract: Brown v. Board of Education marked the beginning of a long era in American politics in which courts, litigation and legal rights were associated with progressive causes. That association, however, is now eroding. The left's discontent with the Supreme Court is well known, but less attention has been paid to liberal concerns about judicial policymaking, including some of the very mechanisms honed by liberals in the Brown erathat go well beyond the Court. The Brown era obscured a simple truth about lawsuits that the next few years are likely to clarify: They are much better at gumming things up than they are at making things work. Policymaking through litigation, though associated with liberals in the Brown era, in fact reflects a deep distrust of centralized governance. Given that it is conservatives, not liberals, who are more often interested in constraining government, this makes lawsuits ordinarily a more congenial policy tool for Republicans than Democrats. For many elements of the Democratic agenda of the next few years, litigation is likely to prove a clumsy tool, more effective in the hands of opponents than proponents.

detail.abstract: The automotive industry is undergoing a profound transformation, driven by the electrification of powertrains, the rise of software-defined vehicles, and the adoption of circular economy concepts. These trends are increasingly blurring the boundaries between the automotive sector and other industries. The pace of adaptation to electrification varies considerably between regions and firms. Unlike internal combustion engine (ICE) production, where mechanical capabilities dominated, competitiveness in electric vehicle (EV) production increasingly depends on expertise in electronics, batteries, and software. This study investigates whether and how firms' ability to leverage cross-industry diversification contributes to their competitive advantage in this evolving landscape. We develop a country-level product space covering all industries, and an industry-specific product space covering over 900 automotive components. This allows us to identify clusters of parts which are exported together, revealing shared manufacturing capabilities. Closeness centrality in the country-level product space, rather than simple proximity, is a strong predictor of where new comparative advantages are likely to emerge. First, we examine this relationship across all industrial sectors to establish general patterns of path dependency, diversification and capability formation. Then, we focus specifically on the electric vehicle (EV) transition. It is argued that new strengths in vehicles and aluminium products in the EU will generate 5 and 4.6 times more EV-specific strengths, respectively, than other EV-relevant sectors over the next decade. In contrast, these sectors are expected to generate only 1.6 and 4.5 new strengths, respectively, in already diversified China. However, a different pattern emerges when these country-level results are compared to the firm-level product space. Countries such as South Korea, China, the US and Canada show the greatest potential for diversification into EV-related products. Established producers in the EU are likely to come under pressure. These findings suggest that the success of the automotive transformation will depend on the ability of regions to mobilize existing industrial capabilities, particularly in related sectors such as machinery and electronic equipment.

title: Structural Uniqueness of the Diffusion Closure : From Kramers-Moyal Expansion to Fokker-Planck Equation

detail.title: Structural Uniqueness of the Diffusion Closure : From Kramers-Moyal Expansion to Fokker-Planck Equation
detail.abstract: The Fokker-Planck equation occupies a structurally distinguished position within the hierarchy of Markov generators: it is the unique finite truncation of the Kramers-Moyal expansion compatible with positivity preservation, empirical identifiability, and stable scaling limits. This paper provides a complete mathematical treatment of this structural uniqueness, including: (i) a rigorous derivation of the Kramers-Moyal expansion with explicit regularity conditions and justified interchange of limits; (ii) a full, self-contained proof of Pawula's theorem on positivity constraints using Fourier-analytic and operator-theoretic methods; (iii) a precise characterization of diffusion as a renormalization group fixed point under space-time rescaling with explicit scaling exponents; (iv) sharp diagnostic criteria with quantified statistical error bounds for empirical validation; and (v) complete proofs of all stated results. We establish that departures from diffusive dynamics signal transitions between universality classes of stochastic processes-to Lévy-type generators when increments have heavy tails, or to non-Markovian kinetic equations when memory effects dominate. The mathematical framework developed here provides both theoretical foundations and practical diagnostic tools for applications in financial econometrics, statistical physics, and machine learning.

detail.abstract: This bibliometric‐systematic research maps five decades of learned helplessness research in human settings across education, mental health, and organizational contexts. Using the B-SLR protocol, we extracted 1,787 peer-reviewed articles (1971–2025) from Web of Science and applied co-occurrence, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, and co-authorship analyses in VOSviewer and CiteSpace. Results reveal five thematic clusters: attributions, motivation, and performance failure; helplessness and mental health; attributional vulnerability and youth depression; neuroscience of control and helplessness; and applied control and empowerment models. Temporal burst analysis identifies an early wave focused on attribution and vulnerable children, a middle wave linking helplessness with health and motivation, and a recent wave emphasizing mental health, neuroscience, and advanced methods. The research consolidates a fragmented literature, clarifies the field’s intellectual structure, and proposes cross-disciplinary directions for interventions that transform learned helplessness into learned hopefulness.

detail.abstract: This article introduces "tool fetishism" as a theoretical concept for analyzing novel forms of alienation in the contemporary gig economy. Returning to Marx's original problematic of commodity fetishism, I argue that when workers legally "reclaim" ownership of their means of production yet fall into deeper alienation, classical fetishism theory requires fundamental extension. Tool fetishism is distinguished by a threefold veiling mechanism: it obscures the global division of labor that produces the instrument, the self-exploitation embedded in its use, and debt's colonization of future time. Integrating Foucault's theory of governmentality with Lazzarato's analysis of the indebted subject, this article further demonstrates how neoliberalism transforms production instruments into material apparatuses for subjectivity production, enabling workers to complete their own disciplining under the illusion of "freedom." The concept of tool fetishism thus opens new analytical terrain for understanding how contemporary capitalism generates consent through the very objects that mediate labor.

detail.abstract: Countercurrent dialysis using hollow fibers presents several advantages over both in-line diafiltration and countercurrent hemodialysis in terms of buffer requirements and compatibility with GMP manufacturing. In this work, we compare GMP-compatible hollow fibers of varying lengths (20 cm, 40 cm and 60 cm) with both in-line diafiltration units (ILDF) and hemodialyzers (F3/F4 low-flux; F180NR high-flux). Both hemodialyzers and hollow fiber units outperformed ILDF in terms of buffer consumption and pressure build-up particularly for higher-titer processes. Furthermore, the hollow fibers showed superior Molecular weight cut off (MWCO) control compared to hemodialyzers while achieving comparable buffer exchange when using endogenous excipients (histidine, methionine) as tracers. A D-optimal experimental design was used to define the design space when varying the ratio of diafiltration buffer to feed flow (“alpha factor” 2–5), feed flux (0.05–1.5 LMH), protein concentration (30–70 mg/mL), and feed conductivity (2–15 mS/cm). The results showed that higher feed concentration narrowed the flux window and required higher alpha factors to achieve the target buffer exchange. Finally, a 5-day run was carried out at the desired process set-point and achieved diafiltration targets along with > 95% yield, no significant impact on aggregation and pressures < 12 psi. Scale-up analysis indicated that the process was suitable for GMP manufacturing to up to 3,000 L scale perfusion bioreactors with perfusate titer ranging from 0.6 – 5 g/L while operating within a robust design space.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a competition between models, GPUs, or training scale, yet these elements exist within a much larger structural system. This paper introduces the Autonomous Economy, a four-layer architecture that explains how value, control, and innovation will be distributed across Infrastructure, Intelligence, Interface, and Human Systems in the Autonomous Age. It expands the scope of the Ragsdale Framework for Autonomous Organizations to encompass global economic and institutional autonomization, and with this expansion, the Framework is renamed the Ragsdale Framework for Autonomization (RFA). Organizational autonomization, including the prior body of RFAO work, becomes one domain within the Interface layer where intelligence meets human workflow. This paper provides the macro-level architecture for autonomization across economies, institutions, and civilizational systems, establishing the foundation for a coordinated research program and inviting outside contributors to participate in its continued development.

detail.abstract: In her influential 2020 review in Globalization and Health, Mialon synthesizes the commercial determinants of health (CDOH) literature and underscores how commercial actors are connected to public health through the institutional environments in which they operate. Much of this research conceptualizes firms as institutionally embedded but relatively homogeneous actors, emphasizing external practices such as the production and promotion of harmful commodities, lobbying, and corporate social responsibility initiatives. While recent CDOH scholarship has begun to recognize the importance of organizational-level factors, few studies analyze the internal processes through which corporate conduct with public health consequences emerges. We argue that integrating insights from management scholarship can enrich CDOH research by opening the “black box” of the firm and clarifying how such conduct arises from interactions among institutional contexts, organizational arrangements, and individual-level dynamics. Drawing on management research, we conceptualize firms as multilevel systems in which institutional conditions inform conduct through organizational governance, resources, and practices, as well as through individual values, cognitions, sensemaking, and interaction among organizational members and stakeholders. These analytically distinct yet dynamically interconnected levels give rise to patterned forms of corporate conduct that affect public health. By foregrounding these multilevel connections, this paper advances a management-informed framework for CDOH research that moves beyond documenting harmful practices toward explaining how firms contribute to public health outcomes and identifying leverage points for intervention.

detail.title: Beyond Paper-Based Ethics in the Digital Feed: The Effects of Short Video App–Guided Loving-Kindness Meditation on Managers’ Empathy, Moral Identity, Sustainability Orientation, and Perceived Ethical Climate
detail.abstract: Background: Corporate governance increasingly relies on ESG policies and compliance architectures, yet “paper-based” ethics often fails to translate into everyday managerial judgment and behavior. Scalable, low-burden internet interventions may help cultivate inner resources that support ethical and sustainability-oriented practice in the workplace.Objective: To evaluate whether an eight-week, short-video app–guided loving-kindness meditation (LKM) program can strengthen managers’ empathic concern, moral identity, sustainability orientation, and perceived ethical climate.Methods: In a two-arm randomized controlled trial, 100 practicing managers were assigned to an app-delivered short-video LKM program or a structurally matched non-LKM control condition. Participants completed validated self-report measures at baseline and post-intervention. Intervention effects were tested using Group (LKM vs. control) × Time (pre vs. post) mixed-design analyses, with the Group × Time interaction as the primary test. Results: Groups were comparable at baseline. Significant Group × Time interactions indicated that managers receiving LKM showed pre–post improvements in empathic concern, moral identity, sustainability orientation, and perceived ethical climate, whereas the control group showed minimal or no change.Conclusions: A brief, short-video app–delivered LKM program embedded in everyday media use may offer a low-burden, scalable internet intervention to enhance socioemotional and prosocial resources relevant to ESG-related practice. Future studies should test longer-term durability and incorporate behavioral and multi-source outcomes.

detail.title: Management earnings forecasts and employee mental health
detail.abstract: This study investigates whether initial management earnings forecasts and their revisions influence employee mental health. We hypothesize that higher management forecasts increase the number of employee resignations related to mental-health issues. Using regression analysis based on 1,953 firm-year observations from Japanese listed firms, we find that firms with higher initial management forecasts experience a higher number of mental health-related resignations. Moreover, we also hypothesize and find that this relationship is strengthened by the frequency and magnitude of management forecast revisions. This study contributes to accounting research on management forecasts by providing evidence of the relationships among initial management forecasts, their revisions, and employee mental health. Our findings suggest the importance of understanding how management-forecasting practices impact employee mental health, shedding light on a significant yet often overlooked social and organizational cost that remains invisible to investors, policy makers and other stakeholders.

detail.abstract: This paper presents Open Health, a federated computing and data platform designed to support new knowledge creation in healthcare. Open Health addresses the growing need to connect and reason across heterogeneous health evidence to enable more innovative, precise, and personalised digital health applications. Open Health is designed to enable four core capabilities within a single platform: (1) integrated data use, by connecting evidence across clinical, genomic, behavioural, social, and environmental domains, spanning electronic health records, medical imaging, genomics and multi-omics, patient-generated data such as wearables and lifestyle measures, biomedical literature, and public health statistics; (2) multistakeholder knowledge creation and use, supporting collaboration among health researchers, clinicians, patients, carers, pharmacists, and other health professionals; (3) personalised and precision medicine, through highly individualised and integrated information, recommendations, and decisions; and (4) data governance by design, implemented through federated analytics that bring algorithms to the data, ensuring that raw data remain under local control while only governed analytical outputs are shared in accordance with regulatory, ethical, and organisational requirements.

detail.abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (aka, LLMs) provides high potential to transform organizational operations, yet a pronounced high interest but low adoption gap persists. Hence, moving beyond individual-level studies to examine organization-wide implementation, we draw on Rogers' innovation decision process and Engeström's activity theory, and conduct in-depth interviews with 27 front-line experts, including LLM providers, adopters, and advisors. Our analysis uncovers ten key contradictions and corresponding practice-driven solutions that emerge across five implementation stages (agenda-setting, matching, redefining and restructuring, clarifying, and routinizing). These insights illuminate not only the multi-stage, socio-technical complexity of LLM deployment but also shifting priorities among activity subsystems and the collaborative mechanisms essential for success. Building on these findings, we offer actionable recommendations for practitioners: a tiered rollout strategy; the technical capability building including decision-support and trial platforms, agile modular architectures and multi-layer update pipelines; as well as an accountable governance framework that integrates internal controls with external accountability. By synthesizing theoretical and practical perspectives, our study intends to guide researchers and business leaders navigate the challenges of organizational LLM implementation and realize their transformative potential at scale.

detail.title: Exploring Misinformation and its Economic Impacts
detail.abstract: Misinformation is a huge hazard to global economies, resulting in financial losses, market instability, and reputational damage. This study explores the various types, sources, and farreaching economic implications of misinformation for individuals, corporations, and governments alike. Misinformation can take many forms, including financial rumours, health-related fallacies, political propaganda, outdated information, and made-up stories. Sources include social media and internet forums, as well as traditional media and private messaging apps. The economic consequences are significant, with misinformation generating market distortions, reduced investor confidence, and supply chain disruptions. It also increases corporate costs, causes financial losses for consumers, and reduces productivity. Misinformation has a negative impact on financial markets, national supply chains, and a country's reputation. The implications are clear from the COVID-19 epidemic, in which misinformation increased economic instability. This study emphasises that to reduce these dangers, investing in media literacy, fact-checking mechanisms, and open public information conduits is critical. By combating misinformation, societies can ensure economic progress, stability, and general well-being.

detail.abstract: Digitization has enabled two-sided platforms to reshape how consumers search for and access professional services that were previously coordinated by incumbent associations. This paper examines the decade-long conflict between LawTalk and the Korean Bar Association, one of the longest and most consequential cases of platform-guild contestation in Korea, and situates it alongside parallel disputes in real estate, tax services, telemedicine, and mobility. Drawing on the analytical lenses of two-sided market theory and differentiated-product competition as well as recent empirical evidence from the legal services market, the paper demonstrates that platform entry in credence goods markets operates primarily by lowering search frictions and widening the product space, rather than by redistributing existing demand. The institutional evolution of the LawTalk case shows how regulatory responses gradually moved away from attempts at exclusion toward a coexistence arrangement that allows digital intermediaries to operate while preserving core professional norms. The paper concludes that policy should prioritize governance of the interface through transparency, auditability, and clear separation between advertising and professional services, rather than relying on categorical restrictions that limit access without improving consumer welfare.

title: Privacy Meets Retrieval: The Performance Consequences of De-Identification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
affiliations: University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management, University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management and University of Minnesota - Twin Cities - Carlson School of Management

detail.title: Privacy Meets Retrieval: The Performance Consequences of De-Identification in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
detail.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a popular technique that integrates large language models (LLMs) with external knowledge corpora to deliver accurate and contextually relevant responses. However, their use in sensitive settings like healthcare raises significant privacy concerns, as both user queries and knowledge corpora can contain private information. While de-identification is commonly used to protect privacy, its impact on the performance of RAG systems remains unexplored. To address this question, we conduct three studies of RAG in the medical domain. Study 1 examines how de-identifying user queries and/or the corpus affects the RAG system's output accuracy through a 2 × 2 factorial experiment and several robustness checks. The results challenge the conventional privacy-utility trade-off by showing that while de-identifying only the query severely degrades performance, de-identifying both the query and the corpus leads to significantly improved accuracy. To further understand this accuracy gain, Study 2 introduces another 2 × 2 factorial experiment and shows that it is mainly driven by the retrieval stage, where alignment between the query and corpus is critical. Study 3 reports that the results are extended to open-ended questions. The findings offer crucial insights for firms and stakeholders developing and deploying privacy-preserving AI systems in healthcare and other sensitive, regulated domains.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has transformed consumer expectations, driving demand for personalized, seamless, and intuitive shopping experiences. This study examines how Artificial Intelligence (AI)–driven personalization influences customer satisfaction, trust, engagement, and loyalty in online shopping environments. Primary data was collected from 100 frequent online shoppers using a structured questionnaire, and analyzed using Microsoft Excel and Power BI to identify patterns, correlations, and predictive relationships. The findings reveal that AI-powered features—such as personalized product recommendations, chatbots, targeted communication, and predictive analytics—significantly enhance customer experience and moderately influence purchase decisions. While consumers generally view AI favorably, concerns related to privacy and accuracy remain. Regression analysis shows that AI personalization positively impacts satisfaction and long-term loyalty, though trust is shaped more strongly by brand reputation and prior positive experiences. Overall, the study concludes that strategic and ethical implementation of AI personalization is essential for e-commerce platforms seeking to strengthen customer relationships, increase engagement, and gain a competitive advantage in the digital marketplace.

title: Structural Defects in Victim Conferral: A Structural Defect Framework for Arizona’s Right to Confer
affiliations: Arizona State University

detail.title: Structural Defects in Victim Conferral: A Structural Defect Framework for Arizona’s Right to Confer
detail.abstract:
Arizona's Victims' Bill of Rights guarantees crime victims the constitutional right to confer with prosecutors before case disposition. Yet the architecture implementing this right—opt-in forms presented at moments of trauma, automated notification pipelines, hallway conferences under docket pressure, and binary minute entries that record only that "conferral occurred"—systematically compresses victim voice in ways current doctrine cannot see or correct. This Article argues that the gap between Arizona's constitutional promise and its procedural delivery is not a failure of individual prosecutors but a structural defect: a foreseeable artifact of architecture designed for low-fidelity output.
Drawing on the Structural Defect Framework developed in parallel work on AI deployment and employment discrimination, this Article provides a diagnostic lens for identifying when recurring harms should be attributed to system design rather than individual error. The Framework's tripartite gateway—fixed interface, nominal equivalence, and supply-chain opacity—explains why conferral's fidelity parameter is structurally invisible. Its four diagnostic elements—structural invisibility, foreseeable harm, doctrinal mismatch, and epistemic asymmetry—demonstrate why the defect persists despite good-faith efforts by individual actors. Arizona's own jurisprudence, which has repeatedly built procedural architecture to reconcile competing constitutional rights, provides the template for reform.
This Article proposes structural guardrails—pre-offer timing requirements, synchronous modality baselines, standardized documentation, and calibrated judicial inquiry—paired with a burden-shifting safe harbor that rewards prosecutors' offices investing in high-fidelity design. The goal is not to grant victims veto power or to indict prosecutors, but to align Arizona's implementation architecture with the constitutional commitments the state has already made. The prosecutor is not the defendant. The architecture is the defendant.

title: Toward Standards for Agentic AI Systems Conceptual Foundations, Trust Boundaries, and Compliance-Aware Design

detail.title: Toward Standards for Agentic AI Systems Conceptual Foundations, Trust Boundaries, and Compliance-Aware Design
detail.abstract: The rapid emergence of agentic artificial intelligence systems has outpaced the development of shared conceptual standards governing their design, trust boundaries, and operational accountability. While recent work has explored individual components such as autonomy, tool use, and orchestration, there remains limited consensus on system-level frameworks that address responsibility, oversight, and compliance in agentic AI deployments. This paper proposes a standards-oriented conceptual framework for agentic AI systems, focusing on role separation, decision authority boundaries, observability, and complianceaware design principles. The objective is not to prescribe specific implementations, but to articulate common abstractions and evaluation criteria that can support interoperability, responsible development, and meaningful review across research and applied settings. Some elements of the underlying invention motivating this work are patent pending. Accordingly, the paper intentionally omits proprietary implementation details and focuses on conceptual structures, terminology, and system-level considerations that can inform ongoing research and standards discussions. The framework is designed to be compatible with current AI systems research while providing a foundation for future empirical and technical validation. By clarifying core concepts and design constraints, this work aims to contribute to the maturation of agentic AI as an engineering discipline, bridging the gap between emerging practice and the need for shared standards.

The millennial generation, known for their adaptability, creativity, and technological literacy, plays a strategic role in driving the digital transformation of MSMEs. This study aims to analyze the technology-based entrepreneurial innovation strategies implemented by millennials and their contribution to increasing MSME creativity in the digital era. detail.abstract: Climate change threatens agricultural productivity in Sub-Saharan Africa, where 95% of cultivated land depends on rain-fed agriculture. Traditional extension systems face critical capacity constraints, with agent-to-farmer ratios averaging 1:1,000, far below the recommended 1:400. This study evaluates the cost-effectiveness of multi-channel weather advisory services as a scalable complementary alternative to conventional extension approaches. We analyze program costs, reach, and behavioral impacts across television, radio, SMS, and community platforms in Kenya and Burkina Faso during 2022-2024. Using the activity-based costing methodology, we assess delivery mechanisms and resource-allocation strategies. The intervention reached 14.5 million farmers with a total investment of USD 551,966, achieving a cost-effectiveness of USD 0.038 per farmer. Mass media channels achieved exceptional cost-efficiency at USD 0.027-0.031 per farmer through broad dissemination, while targeted SMS services provided intensive personalized support at USD 0.60 per farmer. Post-implementation surveys revealed that 83.7% of farmers reported that weather advisories influenced agricultural decision-making, particularly for planting timing, farm activity planning, and crop selection. Results demonstrate that technology-mediated extension can achieve unprecedented scale and cost-effectiveness while maintaining engagement quality. Successful implementation requires strategic integration of technological capabilities with existing agricultural institutions and adaptation to infrastructure dependencies and linguistic contexts. These findings provide empirical evidence for designing scalable climate adaptation interventions in resource-constrained settings.

detail.abstract: AI-mediated mental health interventions have broadened access to psychological support through accessible, high-fluency interfaces. However, the current validation-centric design may contribute to the Metacognitive Bypass Effect, in which AI systems perform the cognitive work of thought restructuring, hindering users from developing independent reality-testing skills. Based on cognitive fluency and error-driven learning theories, two key inhibiting mechanisms are identified: the Polishing Effect, where the refined language of Large Language Models (LLMs) creates unwarranted confidence in distorted cognitions; and the Absence of Productive Struggle, which removes the interpersonal prediction errors needed to internalize cognitive reappraisal skills. To address this, the Metacognitive Scaffolding Model (MSM) is proposed as a phased intervention framework that applies learning science principles to conversational AI. The MSM alternates between validation-focused and challenge-integrated modes, using strategic Socratic questioning and intentional pauses to encourage active self-reflection. Experimental paradigms are described, using metrics such as the Beck Cognitive Insight Scale and new behavioral markers, to assess whether scaffolded cognitive challenge improves long-term skill retention compared to validation-only approaches. This work advocates for a shift in conversational interface design, emphasizing that lasting therapeutic efficacy depends on intentionally incorporating desirable difficulties to support authentic metacognitive development.

detail.abstract: Contemporary institutions operate under unprecedented systemic pressure in which informational turbulence, regulatory compression, geopolitical fragmentation, and cognitive overload redefine the quality of decision-making. detail.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents in multi-agent systems, yet vulnerabilities arising from internal cognitive states remain poorly understood. This study investigates whether minimal personality trait induction through prompt-based manipulation alone can systematically alter negotiation behavior and create exploitable asymmetries between AI agents. We conducted controlled bilateral negotiation experiments where LLM agents induced with Agreeableness or Disagreeableness traits negotiated with unmodified counterparts. Results reveal that personality induction produced substantial performance disparities that depended on agent roles, occurring without any adversarial programming or reward modification. Disagreeable agents leveraged aggressive anchoring and persistent tactics to extract significant value, while Agreeable agents exhibited cooperative vulnerabilities leading to suboptimal outcomes. These behavioral patterns emerged purely from initial trait induction and persisted dynamically throughout interactions. Mediation analysis shows that personality effects propagate through anchoring and concession pathways, while moderation analysis reveals that negotiation duration amplifies or attenuates advantages driven by induced traits depending on the personality type. Our findings demonstrate that asymmetries in internal states constitute a cognitive attack surface where strategies resembling manipulation emerge organically from psychological framing rather than explicit adversarial design. We propose a cognitive assurance framework encompassing persona isolation, behavioral auditing, and cognitive safety testing to address these endogenous vulnerabilities in autonomous AI systems. This work extends AI safety research beyond external threat models to encompass the governance of internal psychological states in AI agents.

detail.abstract: This dissertation investigates the key macroeconomic and structural factors driving graduate unemployment in India from 2011 to 2023. detail.abstract: Welfare services such as healthcare, elderly care, and education are key to ensuring quality of life generally, and vital for rural communities across urbanizing countries. While these sectors are largely tax-financed, several countries have established quasi-markets to achieve competition through private entry to unleash entrepreneurship, efficiency, and service provision innovation. The reforms notwithstanding, productivity improvements are modest, and the situation seems particularly bad in some rural communities. We argue that quasi-markets can only live up to expectations if the local institutional framework considers sectoral and local conditions. While competition and the profit motive are necessary conditions for local quasi-market entrepreneurship and innovation, they are not sufficient but require a set of complementary institutions that are epistemic in nature. These epistemic institutions enable users to make informed choices while simultaneously incentivizing entrepreneurs to compete and innovate along the dimensions that users value. Moreover, if the catchment area includes densely populated areas, rural communities may attract users from communities where costs are higher, thus creating new comparative advantages locally. As an illustration, we analyze the Swedish quasi-market for nursing homes for the elderly.

detail.abstract: Lowering a borrower’s interest rate is one of the most effective ways to reduce a borrower’s debt burden. Mortgage refinancing offers a chance to shift debt balances from high-interest loans into a low-interest mortgage through “cashing out” some of the home’s equity. Using anonymized data on mortgage refinancing behavior, we find that over half of borrowers with high-interest loans and available home equity do not take advantage of their cash-out opportunities. While the cash-out “surcharge” can rationalize this pattern, we leverage a policy change at Fannie Mae that eliminated this surcharge for student-loan borrowers and find that the presence of a student loan does not significantly affect borrowers’ propensity to cash out.
